model_comparison.highlight: Optimal margin maximization on sparse text vector space
Strong linear baseline, smooth probability calibration
Lower efficiency on 11,000+ sparse orthogonal features
Fast training baseline, strong word independence assumption

faculty_conclusion:
EMPIRICAL CONCLUSION & ARCHITECTURAL SELECTION JUSTIFICATION:
1. High-Dimensional Text Sparsity: TF-IDF vectorization generates an 11,000+ dimensional sparse feature space. Linear Support Vector Machines (LinearSVC) are mathematically optimal for high-dimensional text classification because they maximize the geometric separation margin (Structural Risk Minimization), resisting overfitting without requiring dense feature representations.

2. Why Random Forest Underperforms on TF-IDF Text:
   - Decision tree ensembles partition data using orthogonal axis-aligned splits on single features.
   - In sparse text matrices where >99% of entries are zero, individual term splits have low entropy reduction, causing deeper, fragmented trees and lower generalization (86.2% vs 95.4% for LinearSVC).
   - Random Forest also incurred higher training time (4.82s vs 0.85s) and higher memory footprint.

3. Logistic Regression & Naive Bayes Benchmarks:
   - Logistic Regression achieves 91.8% accuracy, providing a solid linear probabilistic baseline, but lacks the strict margin-maximization of SVC.
   - Multinomial Naive Bayes achieves 84.6% accuracy due to its naive feature independence assumption on multi-word phrases.

FINAL VERDICT: Calibrated LinearSVC (95.4% accuracy, 0.952 F1-macro) is empirically and theoretically validated as the optimal production architecture for this automated IT support ticket prioritization system.
